points.text: La capa de enlace de las LAN se divide en dos subcapas: **LLC** (*Logical Link Control*, la superior, común a todos los métodos de acceso e independiente del medio; su servicio orientado a conexión (tipo 2) incluye entrega en secuencia y recuperación de errores) y **MAC** (*Medium Access Control*, propia de cada método de acceso). La norma 802.2 (LLC) se retiró en 2010 en favor de ISO/IEC 8802-2.

refs.title: ISO/IEC 8802-2:1998 (IEEE 802.2) · Logical Link Control (vista previa)
refs.quote: The LLC sublayer constitutes the top sublayer in the data link layer (see figure 1) and is common to the various medium access methods

refs.title: ISO/IEC 8802-2:1998 (IEEE 802.2) · Logical Link Control (vista previa)
refs.quote: Separate International Standards describe each medium access method individually and indicate the additional features and functions that are provided by the Medium Access Control (MAC) sublayer in each case to complete the functionality of the data link layer

refs.title: ISO/IEC 8802-2:1998 (IEEE 802.2) · Logical Link Control (vista previa)
refs.quote: The LLC procedures are independent of the type of medium access method used in the particular LAN.

refs.title: ISO/IEC 8802-2:1998 (IEEE 802.2) · Logical Link Control (vista previa)
refs.quote: This service includes support of sequenced delivery of data link layer data units, and a comprehensive set of data link layer errer recovery techniques

refs.title: IEEE 802.2 Working Group
refs.quote: In 2010, Standard 802.2 was withdrawn by the IEEE.

refs.title: IEEE 802.2 Working Group
refs.quote: Standards should refer to ISO/IEC 8802-2

points.text: **CSMA/CD**: *Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection* (acceso múltiple con detección de portadora y de colisiones), el protocolo MAC de Ethernet para medio compartido (semidúplex).

refs.title: IEEE SA · IEEE 802.3-2022
refs.quote: The Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) MAC protocol specifies shared medium (half duplex) operation, as well as full duplex operation.

points.text: **Tramas jumbo**: mayores que la trama estándar (≈1500 bytes de MTU); **no hay norma** que fije su tamaño; un valor muy extendido es una MTU de **9000 bytes** (p. ej., NFS e iSCSI). Los adaptadores Intel que admiten tramas jumbo llegan a 9216.

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Ethernet Jumbo Frames
refs.quote: There is no industry standard that defines the size of a Jumbo frame

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Ethernet Jumbo Frames
refs.quote: iSCSI SANs (9000 bytes to reduce the effect of TCP frame overhead)

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Ethernet Jumbo Frames
refs.quote: a single 9000 byte MTU jumbo frame replaces six 1500 byte MTU standard frames

refs.title: Intel · Ethernet Adapters User Guide: Jumbo Frames
refs.quote: Intel adapters that support Jumbo Packets have a frame size limit of 9238 bytes, with a corresponding MTU size limit of 9216 bytes.

points.text: **Estrella**: un **nodo central** con la función de control conecta a todos los demás, y toda la comunicación pasa por él.

refs.title: IEC Electropedia · IEV 351-56-12 (red en estrella)
refs.quote: in which one centre with network control function provides connections between all the other participants without network control function and organizes the communication, which is handled exclusively via the control centre

points.text: **Anillo**: camino de transmisión **circular**; cada equipo pasa los datos que no son para él a su **vecino siguiente**: los datos circulan de un equipo al siguiente.

refs.title: IEC Electropedia · IEV 351-56-11 (red en anillo)
refs.quote: via a common, circular transmission path, whereby each participant is able to pass on data that do not concern itself to its subsequent neighbour

points.text: **POL / POLAN** (LAN óptica pasiva): red **GPON** con **fibra monomodo** hasta un **divisor óptico pasivo** (sin alimentación), entre el equipo central (**OLT**) y los terminales de usuario (**ONT**), que convierten a Ethernet.

refs.title: APOLAN · Passive Optical LAN Technical Specification, Division 27.0 (2022)
refs.quote: The Passive Optical LAN also referred to as Gigabit Passive Optical Network (GPON)

refs.title: APOLAN · Passive Optical LAN Technical Specification, Division 27.0 (2022)
refs.quote: Optical Line Terminal (OLT) or Headend Equipment: The equipment that connects to the network core, aggregates services, and distributes across the single-mode optical fiber to the Optical Network Terminal

refs.title: APOLAN · Passive Optical LAN Technical Specification, Division 27.0 (2022)
refs.quote: Optical Network Terminal (ONT) or end user device: The equipment that receives communication signals from the OLT and then converts media to Ethernet

refs.title: APOLAN · Passive Optical LAN Technical Specification, Division 27.0 (2022)
refs.quote: Passive: Component that does not require AC/DC power for operation

refs.title: APOLAN · Passive Optical LAN Technical Specification, Division 27.0 (2022)
refs.quote: Optical fiber-based technology that relies on singlemode fiber backhaul to a passive optical splitter

points.text: **Concentrador (hub)**: capa 1 (física); repite la señal por los demás puertos, y todos ellos forman **un único dominio de colisión**.

refs.title: Cisco · Troubleshoot LAN Switching Environments
refs.quote: In terms of the OSI model, a hub is considered a layer-one (physical layer) device. It hears an electrical signal on the wire and passes it along to the other ports.

refs.title: Cisco Networking Academy · CCNA2 capítulo 1 (material del curso)
refs.quote: All ports of a hub belong to the same collision domain.

points.text: **Conmutador (switch)**: capa 2; funciona como un puente. Cada puerto es **su propio dominio de colisión**, pero reenvía las difusiones a todos los puertos: mantiene **un único dominio de difusión** (salvo que se usen VLAN, cada una un dominio de difusión).

refs.title: Cisco · Troubleshoot LAN Switching Environments
refs.quote: A basic switch is considered a layer-two device.

refs.title: Cisco · Troubleshoot LAN Switching Environments
refs.quote: Logically, a switch acts just like a transparent bridge would

refs.title: Cisco Networking Academy · CCNA2 capítulo 1 (material del curso)
refs.quote: Every port of a switch is a collision domain on its own.

refs.title: Cisco Networking Academy · CCNA2 capítulo 1 (material del curso)
refs.quote: Switches forward broadcast frames to all ports; therefore, switches do not break broadcast domains.

refs.title: Cisco · Troubleshoot LAN Switching Environments
refs.quote: VLANs are also described as broadcast domains.

points.text: **Encaminador (router)**: pasarela entre redes en la **capa 3** de OSI; dirige los paquetes de una red a otra.

refs.title: NIST CSRC Glossary · router
refs.quote: A computer that is a gateway between two networks at OSI layer 3 and that relays and directs data packets through that inter-network.

points.text: **Pasarela (gateway)**: conecta redes con **arquitecturas y protocolos distintos**.

refs.title: IEC Electropedia · IEV 732-01-17 gateway (pasarela)
refs.quote: functional unit that connects two computer networks with different network architectures and protocols

points.text: **VLAN** (802.1Q): cada VLAN tiene un identificador único. En los puertos troncales (**tagged**) las tramas llevan la **etiqueta 802.1Q con el VLAN ID**; los puertos de acceso (**untagged**) solo aceptan tramas sin etiqueta. Para pasar de una VLAN a otra hace falta encaminamiento (capa 3): un router o un conmutador con interfaz de capa 3 (IRB en Juniper).

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: When an Ethernet LAN is divided into VLANs, each VLAN is identified by a unique 802.1Q ID.

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: The packet also has a VLAN ID field that includes the unique 802.1Q ID, which identifies the VLAN to which the packet belongs.

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: Access interfaces accept only untagged packets.

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: Trunk interfaces usually accept only tagged packets and use the VLAN ID tag to determine both the packets’ VLAN origin and VLAN destination.

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: Switches perform inter-VLAN routing functions using an integrated routing and bridging (IRB) interface named irb.

refs.title: Juniper · Bridging and VLANs
refs.quote: Traditionally, switches sent traffic to hosts that were part of the same broadcast domain (VLAN) but routers were needed to route traffic from one broadcast domain to another.

points.text: **RSTP** (*Rapid Spanning Tree*) es **IEEE 802.1w**, evolución de 802.1D para reconfigurar el árbol rápidamente; se incorporó a 802.1D-2004.

refs.title: Cisco · Understand Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (802.1w)
refs.quote: Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP; IEEE 802.1w) can be seen as an evolution of the 802.1D standard more than a revolution.

refs.title: Cisco · Understand Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (802.1w)
refs.quote: The new edition of the 802.1D standard, IEEE 802.1D-2004, incorporates IEEE 802.1t-2001 and IEEE 802.1w standards.

refs.title: IEEE 802.1 · 802.1w Rapid Reconfiguration of Spanning Tree
refs.quote: 802.1w - Rapid Reconfiguration of Spanning Tree

points.text: Normas PoE: **802.3af** (2003, 13 W en el dispositivo; Tipo 1), **802.3at** (2009, 25,5 W; Tipo 2) y **802.3bt** (2018, la tercera, posterior a af y at; permite usar **los cuatro pares**, obligatorio desde la clase 5, y define los **Tipos 3** (hasta 51 W) **y 4** (hasta **71,3 W** en el dispositivo, 90 W en la fuente)). Para una sonda de unos 70 W hace falta 802.3bt.

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Overview of 802.3bt - Power over Ethernet standard
refs.quote: The new Power over Ethernet 802.3bt standard is the third revision to the widely adopted IEEE standard that specifies low voltage power transfer to networked devices.

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Overview of 802.3bt - Power over Ethernet standard
refs.quote: The first IEEE PoE standard, 802.3af (2003), was able to provide 13 W to devices. This was increased to 25.5 W by 802.3at (2009). With 802.3bt, the amount of power available for devices increases nearly threefold, to 71.3 W

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Overview of 802.3bt - Power over Ethernet standard
refs.quote: Type 1 refers to the 802.3af specification, whereas 802.3at introduced Type 2

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Overview of 802.3bt - Power over Ethernet standard
refs.quote: For assigned Class 5 and higher, power delivery requires 4 pairs to be used.

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · Overview of 802.3bt - Power over Ethernet standard
refs.quote: 802.3bt introduces two new Types: Type 3, which supports up to 51 W delivered to a PD, and Type 4, which supports up to 71.3 W delivered to a PD.

refs.title: Ethernet Alliance · 802.3bt (presentación)
refs.quote: IEEE 802.3bt PSE=90W Type 4 PD=71W

refs.title: IEEE SA · IEEE 802.3bt-2018
refs.quote: The maximum Powered Device (PD) power available is increased by this amendment to IEEE Std 802.3-2018 by utilizing all four pairs in the specified structured wiring plant.
